body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 6 models with a format search (of 279 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.6 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 4 of 6 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 43.3 → 71.2, higher is worse), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 66%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 67%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB), groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB), add output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.2 dB), conv2d bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.6 dB) and div output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 36.9 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): mul outputs end furthest from full precision, facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 keeping only -0.8 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), linear in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 9.0 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), softmax in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 9.8 dB), add in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 10.0 dB), gelu in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 10.2 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB) and attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 2737 (59%), fp8_e3m4 1097 (24%), fp8_e1m6 771 (17%); 0% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.4 dB) and upsample in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.9 dB).

1 missing capability keep 29 operations in 1 model (of 4 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (29 operations in 1 model). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 29 operations in 1 model: 29 calls (1.32% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256. Cost today: 0 of 29 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 29 wait for one; 0 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

title: Missing instructions: 29 operations in 1 model need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 369 of 659 tensors passed between kernels (56%) in 4 models: 207 for attention heads split or merged, 142 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 231 operations (231 calls, 11% of all calls; 98.5 G MACs, 4.22% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → add (other reshapes) 58 and linear → mul (other reshapes) 56; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (33).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 369 of 659 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 656 operations in 4 models (656 calls, 30% of all calls), most often silu (210), layernorm (126) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst 9.2 dB SQNR over 656 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 50.5, most 81 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 81 planned groups), over 4 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 34.4 powers of ten for mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (largest value 1.48e+04).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 656 operations limited by the LUT and up to 81 kernel launches per pass

body: The most costly finding is layout conversion: 357 of 583 tensors (61%) passed between kernels must be rearranged by the reading kernel, affecting 219 calls (11% of calls, 14% of MACs), though the cycle cost is unmeasured. Next is quantisation accuracy under NX8 formats: model outputs lose a median 21.3 dB SQNR (worst 7.4 dB), 3 of 4 models lose prediction agreement, and the worst single tensors are layernorm, add and mul outputs in DiT-XL-2-256 (best ~32–34 dB), with mul output in DiT-XL-2-256 also worst for accumulated path error (-0.8 dB). Then resource limits: 550 operations (28% of calls) go through the 256-entry LUT, limiting their precision (worst 9.2 dB SQNR), and kernel launches per pass reach a median of 58 and a maximum of 81. Least costly is the missing run-time addressing instruction: 29 embedding calls (1.48% of calls, no MACs) in one model need workarounds, none of which exist yet, and adding the instruction would run them directly. Compute efficiency (MAC utilisation) and instruction memory use are not yet measured, so their costs are unknown.
title: GLM summary

body: **Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 29 operations in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 29 calls (1.32% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
